study type: Quality Improvement Study (Retrospective and Prospective Cohort Components)
exposure: Delayed Cord Clamping (DCC) + Minimally Invasive Surfactant Administration (MISA)
Immediate Cord Clamping (ICC) + Minimally Invasive Surfactant Administration (MISA)
Immediate Cord Clamping (ICC) + Tracheal Intubation-based Surfactant Delivery
cohort: The study participants are neonates with Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (NRDS) born at a gestational age of less than 30 weeks.
finding: The study aims to determine if the combined use of Delayed Cord Clamping (DCC) and Minimally Invasive Surfactant Administration (MISA) offers greater benefits in improving the prognosis and reducing the incidence of BPD in very premature infants compared to other treatment strategies.
